name: Space.card_classes_le
summary: For each class g pick a short basis Y_g with g.out⁻¹Y_g integral, the Gram matrix G_g = Y_g*Y_g, and an approximation X_g ∈ Mat_n(E) of (g.out⁻¹Y_g)⁻¹ modulo Ô with small archimedean entries. The entries of G_g and G_gX_g are algebraic integers bounded by C³ at every infinite place, and they determine the class: equal entries give a rational unitary γ = Y_gY_{g'}⁻¹ and an integral κ relating the representatives. The count of such integral vectors (Filling.encard_integral_le) gives the bound.

steps.claim: For every class g (with its chosen representative g.out ∈ G_f) choose Y_g ∈ GL_n(E) with g.out⁻¹·Y_g integral (l) and |φ((Y_g)_{ij})| ≤ C for every complex embedding φ of E and all i, j (hY).
steps.lean: choose Y l hY using fun g : StdClasses (Kf E n) ↦ exists_short_basis_stdSpace h g.out

steps.claim: Let A_g = g.out⁻¹·Y_g (an integral matrix over the finite adeles) and G_g = Y_g*·1·Y_g ∈ GL_n(E), the Gram matrix of the columns of Y_g for the standard form.
steps.lean: let A g := g.out⁻¹.1 * (Y g).map (algebraMap ..); let G g := star (Y g) * 1 * Y g

steps.claim: For every finite adele y choose r(y) ∈ E with y − r(y) ∈ Ô (o) and |Φ_w(r(y))| ≤ (2f)²·N at every infinite place w (hr) (exists_rat_near_of_mem_differentIdeal with d = N ≠ 0 and z = 0).
steps.lean: choose r o hr using exists_rat_near_of_mem_differentIdeal NeZero.out h 0

steps.claim: Let X_g ∈ Mat_n(E) be r applied entrywise to A_g⁻¹ (an approximation of A_g⁻¹ modulo Ô).
For all classes g, g': A_{g'}A_g⁻¹ − A_{g'}X_g = A_{g'}(A_g⁻¹ − X_g) is integral (new o g g'), as A_{g'} is integral (l) and A_g⁻¹ − X_g is integral entrywise (o).
steps.lean: replace o g g' := mul_sub (A _).1 _ ((X g).map (↑)) ▸ (l g').mul (by tauto)

steps.claim: Count by an injective map into integral vectors: the number of classes is the ncard of the whole set, and Filling.encard_integral_le, applied to g ↦ (entries of G_g·X_g and of G_g·1, indexed by Bool × n × n) with r = C³, bounds it by (1 + 2C³)^{2|n|²·f·2} = (1 + 2C³)^{4f|n|²} (the exponent identity by `simp; ring`). Three goals remain: (a) these entries are algebraic integers; (b) their absolute values at every infinite place are at most C³; (c) two classes g', g whose vectors agree (e) are equal, which follows from the double coset relation between their representatives.
steps.lean:
refine Set.ncard_univ _ ▸ .trans_eq (ENat.toNat_le_of_le_natCast
    (mod_cast Filling.encard_integral_le (fun g (k, i, j) ↦
    (G g * cond k (X g) 1) i j) (shortBasisConst E n N ^ 3).cast_nonneg (fun g _ (k, i, j)
    ↦ ⟨?_, fun _ ↦ ?_⟩) fun g' _ g _ e ↦ Quotient.out_equiv_out.1 (rel_iff.2 ?_))) (by simp; ring)

steps.claim: In goal (a), unfold G_g and reassociate the products.

Claim b: for a matrix B over E such that g.out⁻¹·B is integral, the entries of Y_g*·B are integral: since g.out⁻¹ is unitary, Y_g*·B = (g.out⁻¹Y_g)*·(g.out⁻¹B) = A_g*·1·(g.out⁻¹B), a product of integral matrices.
steps.lean: have b {B} := (U.gram_invariant g.out⁻¹ _ B ▸ ((l _).isInt_conjTranspose.mul .one).mul · i j)

steps.claim: Goal (a), in both cases of the Bool index: for G_g·1 apply b to B = Y_g (A_g integral, l); for G_g·X_g apply b to B = Y_g·X_g, as g.out⁻¹Y_gX_g = A_gX_g = 1 − (A_gA_g⁻¹ − A_gX_g) is integral (step 5 with g' = g); an element of E that is integral at every finite place is an algebraic integer.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨⟨⟩⟩ := k, b (l _), b (by simpa [A, mul_assoc, ↓val_inv] using IsIntMatrix.one.sub (o g
    g)) <;> simp_all [mul_apply, ← algebraMap_mem_Ô]

steps.claim: Goal (b), in both cases of the Bool index (n is nonempty, as it has the index i): expand the entries as sums and use the triangle inequality, |Φ_v((Y_g)_{ab})| ≤ C (hY) and |Φ_v(r(·))| ≤ (2f)²N (hr): |Φ_v((G_g)_{ij})| ≤ |n|·C² and |Φ_v((G_gX_g)_{ij})| ≤ |n|²·C²·(2f)²N, both at most C³ = (6N f²|n|²)³ since N, f, |n| ≥ 1.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨⟨⟩⟩ := k, Inhabited.mk i <;> simp_all [mul_apply, X, G] <;>
  · repeat grw [norm_sum_le] <;> simp
    grw [hY, hY]; try grw [hr]
    simp; ring_nf; gcongr <;> norm_num [NeZero.one_le]

steps.claim: Goal (c): read e entrywise: G_{g'} = G_g (the Bool index false) and G_{g'}X_{g'} = G_gX_g (the index true).

The double coset relation: γ = Y_g·Y_{g'}⁻¹ is unitary for the standard form (from G_{g'} = G_g by gram_inv_of_gram_eq and gram_mul_of_gram_eq), hence a rational point in Γ_f; and κ = A_{g'}·A_g⁻¹ = g'.out⁻¹·γ⁻¹·g.out lies in K_f (mem_Kf): G_g is invertible, so G_gX_g = G_{g'}X_{g'} = G_gX_{g'} gives X_g = X_{g'}, and then A_{g'}A_g⁻¹ = 1 + (A_{g'}A_g⁻¹ − A_{g'}X_g) − (A_{g'}A_{g'}⁻¹ − A_{g'}X_{g'}) is integral (step 5 twice). Hence g.out = γ·g'.out·κ.
steps.lean:
exact ⟨_, ⟨⟨_, gram_mul_of_gram_eq rfl (gram_inv_of_gram_eq e.1)⟩, rfl⟩, _, by
    simpa [mem_Kf, A, ↓val_inv, mul_assoc, (G _).mul_right_inj.1 (e.1 ▸ e.2)]
      using! IsIntMatrix.one.add ((o g g').sub (o g' g')), eq_mul_of_inv_mul_eq rfl⟩
